The vulnerability: `flb_utils_time_to_seconds` reads `time[len - 1]` — if `len == 0` (empty string), it reads `time[-1]`, which is an out-of-bounds read (heap-buffer-underflow if the string is heap-allocated at the start of a buffer).

The fuzzer `utils_fuzzer.c` passes `null_terminated` (heap-allocated with malloc(size+1)) to `flb_utils_time_to_seconds`. But wait — the input is null-terminated from `data` of size >= 600. If the first byte of data is '\0', then `strlen(null_terminated) == 0`, and `time[-1]` reads one byte before the heap buffer → heap-buffer-underflow detected by ASAN.
